report:
All 13 windows are graded and stored: 13 accepted, 0 rejected, confirmed with `label get judgment`.

**Episodes found (Thompson_Thompson_100, a crowded tailgate where the robot mostly walks behind groups of people)**

Speeds below are the smoothed speed from `signals`. Each person sighting was checked on a full-resolution frame.

| Speed-up | Speed | New person before it? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 146.35–147.54 s | 0.77→1.19 m/s | Yes: a person in a grey hoodie walks towards the robot in the path ahead at ~144.5 s (`image#4284`), then passes on the right | **Qualifies** |
| 148.81–150.74 s | 0.885→1.43 m/s | Yes: a man in a white jacket appears ahead-right at ~147.5 s, walking towards the robot (`image#4380`) | **Qualifies** |
| 195.3–197.09 s | 0.62→0.97 m/s | Yes: a man in a black jacket appears ahead-left at ~194.5 s, walking towards the robot (`image#5787`) | **Qualifies**, though the robot is also following a couple |
| 73.55–74.61 s | 0.95→1.33 m/s | Unclear: a group walks across the grass ahead-left, off the path (`image#2137`) | **Ambiguous** |
| 98.83–100.35 s | 0.68→1.12 m/s | No: same group it has followed since 94 s (`image#2896`) | Near-miss |
| 166.13–167.69 s | 0.97→1.47 m/s | No: everyone ahead was already visible at 164 s (`image#4920`) | Near-miss |
| 60.35–61.87 s | 0.64→1.19 m/s | No: the speed-up comes as the crowd clears; everyone ahead was visible since 58.5 s | Near-miss, and 1.35 s after window 59 anyway |

**Grade counts:** 7 × 2 (windows 147–152 and 200), 1 × 1 (window 76), 5 × 0 (windows 36, 59, 100, 168, 204), and no −1.

**What the data can't establish (for `answered_partial`)**
- **"A new person appears" isn't well defined in a dense crowd.** People enter the camera view almost every second, so the time part of the intent is met nearly everywhere. I only counted a person who newly appears in or next to the path, a few metres ahead, within about 2 s before the speed-up. Window 76 got a 1 because it only has off-path people.
- **Is the order enough, or must the person cause it?** "Shortly after" can't tell a speed-up caused by a new person from one that just keeps pace with people the robot is following. Window 200 and the 146–151 s episodes meet the timing, but the walkers being followed may be what really drives the speed. I read the intent as timing only; a stricter causal reading would drop those to 1.
- **"In front of it" has no distance or angle given**, so I judged it by eye from the camera frames rather than by a lidar distance limit.

The batch file is `annotations/tmp/l2-test_speedup_after_person-v9-p3/batch_1.json`.
